prompt: A fair die has an expected value of 3.5, but no face shows 3.5. What does the expectation describe?

options.text: An impossible model because averages must be outcomes.
options.explanation: Averages can lie between possible values.

options.text: A guarantee that every short batch averages exactly 3.5.
options.explanation: Finite samples vary around the expectation.

options.text: The probability-weighted average, approached by sample means under repeated independent fair rolls.
options.explanation: An expectation need not be an attainable individual observation.

options.text: The face most likely on the next roll.
options.explanation: All six faces are equally likely.

workedExample: An individual roll selects one face; averaging combines many values with their probabilities. The law of large numbers supports convergence of independent repeated averages, without making any one run deterministic.
